findings.title: IPv4-mapped IPv6 block is entirely dead code — every branch already returns above
findings.problem: Python's ipaddress.IPv6Address already delegates is_loopback / is_link_local / is_unspecified / is_multicast to the embedded IPv4 address for ::ffff:0:0/96. Verified by execution: ipaddress.ip_address('::ffff:127.0.0.1').is_loopback is True, and likewise for ::ffff:169.254.169.254 (link-local), ::ffff:0.0.0.0 (unspecified) and ::ffff:224.0.0.1 (multicast). So line 82 already returns (False, 'Blocked address') for every input the new block at 85-88 would catch, and the inner if can never be True on any address that reaches line 85. The four new tests (tests/test_validation.py:93-109) pass because of line 82, not because of the new code — they would pass identically with lines 84-88 deleted. Not itself a security hole (behavior is correct), but it is a branch that can never execute, and it creates a false sense that the D-10 mapped-address case is handled by dedicated logic when it is really handled incidentally by the base check.
findings.fix_hint: Either delete lines 84-88 as redundant, or repurpose the mapped-address unwrapping to do the thing the base check does NOT do — re-run the BLOCKED_HOSTS string check against str(addr.ipv4_mapped) (see bugs-002)
findings.why_it_matters: Dead code in a security path invites a future maintainer to trust it for coverage it does not actually provide, and the accompanying tests give false confidence that the mapped-address path is independently exercised.

findings.title: BLOCKED_HOSTS metadata check still bypassable via IPv4-mapped IPv6 form
findings.problem: The new code unwraps ipv4_mapped but only re-tests the four ipaddress properties — it never re-tests BLOCKED_HOSTS. The string check at line 77 compares the raw hostname, which for 'http://[::ffff:100.100.100.200]:7878' is the literal '::ffff:100.100.100.200' (verified via urlparse) and does not match the '100.100.100.200' entry in BLOCKED_HOSTS. That Alibaba-cloud metadata IP has none of is_link_local/is_loopback/is_unspecified/is_multicast set, and 100.100.100.200 is not in any special-use range, so it passes validation. metadata.google.internal / metadata.azure.com are hostnames and unaffected; 169.254.169.254 happens to be caught only because it is link-local. So the diff adds a mapped-address unwrap that misses precisely the case where unwrapping would have mattered.
findings.fix_hint: inside the ipv4_mapped branch, also check `str(mapped) in BLOCKED_HOSTS` and return (False, "Blocked hostname")
findings.why_it_matters: An operator-supplied URL of the form http://[::ffff:100.100.100.200] reaches the Alibaba metadata service through the *arr HTTP client, defeating the stated purpose of BLOCKED_HOSTS.

findings.title: SSRF bypass via NAT64-embedded IPv4 addresses not blocked
findings.problem: The new `ipv4_mapped` check only catches the standard IPv4-mapped IPv6 form (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`). It does not catch IPv4-embedded addresses under the NAT64/DNS64 well-known prefix `64:ff9b::/96` (RFC 6052), e.g. `64:ff9b::169.254.169.254` (encoded as `64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe`). `ipaddress.IPv6Address.ipv4_mapped` returns `None` for this form, and none of `is_link_local`/`is_loopback`/`is_unspecified`/`is_multicast` catch it either, so this literal sails through `validate_arr_url` untouched. On networks/hosts with NAT64/DNS64 enabled (common in IPv6-only or dual-stack container/cloud environments), the underlying httpx client resolving/connecting to this address would reach the embedded IPv4 target, i.e. cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) or other blocked hosts, defeating the SSRF guard.
findings.fix_hint: Also extract and check the embedded IPv4 for the NAT64 well-known prefix (64:ff9b::/96) — e.g. check `addr in ipaddress.ip_network('64:ff9b::/96')` and unpack the low 32 bits as an IPv4Address for the same is_link_local/is_loopback/is_unspecified/is_multicast checks; consider generalizing to a helper that tries both the mapped and NAT64 extraction paths.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the exact vulnerability class the diff is fixing (IP-literal encoding tricks bypassing the blocklist), just via a different well-known IPv6 prefix. An attacker configuring the *arr URL field could target cloud metadata services or internal-only hosts on a NAT64-enabled deployment, potentially exfiltrating cloud credentials.

findings.title: Mapped-address branch enforces the property blocklist but skips BLOCKED_HOSTS — two SSRF policy sources out of sync

intent_doc_match.quote: D-10: Add IPv4-mapped IPv6 address checks to `validate_arr_url`. Check `addr.ipv4_mapped` on IPv6 addresses and validate the mapped address against the same blocklist. Also block multicast addresses.

findings.problem: validate_arr_url now enforces its SSRF policy through two parallel mechanisms that are not kept in sync: a string-literal hostname blocklist (BLOCKED_HOSTS, line 18/77) and an ipaddress property blocklist (lines 82-88). The new IPv4-mapped branch replicates the property list for the mapped address but does NOT re-check the mapped address against BLOCKED_HOSTS. Verified by execution: urlparse('http://[::ffff:100.100.100.200]:7878').hostname -> '::ffff:100.100.100.200' misses the BLOCKED_HOSTS string match, and its ipv4_mapped form 100.100.100.200 (Alibaba metadata) has is_link_local/is_loopback/is_unspecified/is_multicast all False, so validate_arr_url returns (True, ''). The same holds for the hex spelling ::ffff:6464:64c8. (169.254.169.254 and metadata.google.internal are incidentally covered because the mapped form happens to be link-local, so the gap is only visible for the non-link-local metadata entries.) Architecturally, the diff extended one of the two policy sources and left the other behind; the fix belongs at the design level — normalize the hostname to a canonical address once (unwrap ipv4_mapped, and note ipaddress also parses IPv4-compatible ::a9fe:a9fe forms) and then run a single blocklist over the normalized value, rather than duplicating a check list per address shape.
findings.fix_hint: Normalize before checking instead of duplicating the check list: after ipaddress.ip_address(hostname), unwrap `addr = addr.ipv4_mapped or addr` into a single canonical address, then run one guard covering both the property set and `str(addr) in BLOCKED_HOSTS`. If the mapped-vs-direct distinction must stay, at minimum add `str(mapped) in BLOCKED_HOSTS` to the mapped branch and a test for 'http://[::ffff:100.100.100.200]:7878'.
findings.why_it_matters: 59-CONTEXT.md D-10 says to validate the mapped address 'against the same blocklist'; the implementation validated it against the same property checks but not against BLOCKED_HOSTS, so a future blocklist entry can again apply to only one address spelling.

findings.title: IPv4-mapped IPv6 bypass of BLOCKED_HOSTS metadata allowlist remains open
findings.problem: The new ipv4_mapped block re-checks only the four ipaddress property flags (is_link_local/is_loopback/is_unspecified/is_multicast). It never re-checks the mapped address against BLOCKED_HOSTS (line 18), which is a string-literal set matched against the raw hostname earlier at line 77. Cloud metadata endpoints that are NOT link-local therefore survive the IPv4-mapped form. Verified by executing the changed function against .venv/bin/python: validate_arr_url('http://[::ffff:100.100.100.200]') returns (True, '') while validate_arr_url('http://100.100.100.200') returns (False, 'Blocked hostname'). 100.100.100.200 is the Alibaba Cloud metadata service and is explicitly listed in BLOCKED_HOSTS, so the bypass D-10 was written to close is still open for that entry. 169.254.169.254 happens to be caught, but only incidentally because 169.254/16 is link-local -- not because BLOCKED_HOSTS was consulted. Blast radius is narrow: the only caller is the authenticated settings-save handler at triggarr/web/routes.py:522, so exploitation requires an authenticated admin (or CSRF against one) rather than an anonymous request.
findings.fix_hint: Also test `str(mapped) in BLOCKED_HOSTS` inside the ipv4_mapped branch (and add a test for `http://[::ffff:100.100.100.200]`).
findings.why_it_matters: The stated purpose of this diff (D-10 / SHIELD-007) is to stop SSRF reaching internal endpoints via the IPv4-mapped IPv6 encoding. One of the four hosts the codebase explicitly enumerates as must-block is still reachable through exactly that encoding, so the mitigation is incomplete against its own threat model entry T-59-04.

findings.title: Apply the explicit blocklist to mapped IPv4 addresses
findings.problem: The new mapped-address branch checks address categories but never checks BLOCKED_HOSTS. Confirmed locally: http://100.100.100.200 is rejected, while http://[::ffff:100.100.100.200] is accepted. Settings therefore still accept a mapped representation of an explicitly blocked metadata endpoint. On deployments where that endpoint is reachable through IPv4 mapping, this leaves the SSRF protection incomplete.
findings.fix_hint: Reject mapped addresses when str(mapped) is in BLOCKED_HOSTS, in addition to the category checks. Add regression tests for dotted and hexadecimal mapped representations of 100.100.100.200.
